sentences.text: The short issue before this Court is with respect to the classification of the said property.
The respondent authorities have classified the properties as a wetland, without road access.

The learned counsel would submit that in the settlement deed, under which the petitioners are claiming, a clear, well-laid private pathway has been provided for access to the properties of the petitioners, and that private road is abutting another municipal road.

Therefore, their property cannot be treated as a wetland,
without road access, is the sum and substance of the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners.

2. Learned Government Pleader would not dispute that WP(C) Nos.9963/2025, 9990/2025 10013/2025, 10119/2025 6 2025:KER:85024 there is a private way providing access to the petitioners' property, and that the said private way abuts the municipal road.
3. If that be the situation, the petitioners are well within their limits to urge that their property cannot be treated as one without road access.
The properties are liable to be treated as one with road access.
It is not the mandate of law that, for a property being treated as one with road access should necessarily have road access to a municipal road.

If the properties having an access to a private road,
which, in turn, leads to a municipal road, the same is also liable to be treated as a properties having road access.

4. As regards the second contention raised by the learned Government Pleader that the petitioners have to prefer a reference under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, this Court is WP(C) Nos.9963/2025,
9990/2025 10013/2025, 10119/2025 7 2025:KER:85024 of the opinion that, having regard to the short issue which has already been discussed above, the petitioners need not be relegated to that course.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is also trite that the existence of the statutory remedy is not always a bar for exercising a Writ Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

5. In the circumstances, there will be a direction to the 3rd respondent-Tahsildar to treat the petitioners' property as one with private road access, and to fix the compensation accordingly, at the time of passing the Order.
All necessary corrections pursuant to the above direction will have to be made by the 3rd respondent.
These Writ Petitions are disposed of as above.
